blocks.content: A PV's reclaim policy decides what actually happens to the underlying storage once its bound PVC is deleted, this is a genuinely consequential setting, worth understanding precisely before it surprises you.
1. Retain: Keep the Data, Manual Cleanup
blocks.text: 1. Retain: Keep the Data, Manual Cleanup

blocks.content: Retain keeps the underlying storage and its data fully intact after the PVC is deleted, the PV moves to a Released state, but is not automatically reused or deleted, an administrator has to explicitly decide what to do with it next.

blocks.alt: Nothing is lost, but nothing is automatically cleaned up either

blocks.content: 2. Delete: the Underlying Storage Is Actually Removed
blocks.text: 2. Delete: the Underlying Storage Is Actually Removed

blocks.content: Delete is more aggressive, the moment the PVC is deleted, the actual underlying storage resource (the real cloud disk) is deleted too, this is genuinely destructive and irreversible.

blocks.alt: A real, irreversible deletion of the actual underlying storage

blocks.content:
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: pv-data
spec:
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain   # deliberately not Delete, for important data

code.content:

codes.yaml:

kind: PersistentVolume

  name: pv-data
spec:
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain   # deliberately not Delete, for important data

blocks.content: An older policy, Recycle, used to scrub a volume's data and make it available for reuse, it is deprecated and not used in modern Kubernetes, worth recognizing the term for historical context, not something to actually configure.

blocks.alt: A deprecated policy, only worth recognizing, not using

blocks.content: 4. The Common Default for Dynamically Provisioned Storage
blocks.text: 4. The Common Default for Dynamically Provisioned Storage

blocks.content: This is genuinely important to know: PVs created via dynamic provisioning, covered in the previous topic, very often default to the Delete policy, meaning deleting the PVC that requested them can silently delete the real underlying data too.

blocks.alt: A default that quietly deletes real data, unless you know to check it

blocks.content: 5. Why This Matters as a Real Risk
blocks.text: 5. Why This Matters as a Real Risk

blocks.content: Someone deleting a PVC assuming it is a safe, reversible cleanup step, without realizing its PV is set to Delete, can genuinely and permanently lose production data, this is exactly the kind of setting worth checking explicitly before deleting any PVC you did not personally provision.

blocks.alt: A genuine data-loss risk, worth checking before deleting any PVC

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Retain keeps the underlying storage and requires manual cleanup, Delete actually destroys the underlying storage, Recycle is deprecated and no longer used.
Dynamically provisioned PVs often default to Delete, a real, easy-to-miss data-loss risk worth explicitly checking before ever deleting a PVC.
